newsitem.title: GERMANY: German bank merger offer period kicks offs.
newsitem.headline: German bank merger offer period kicks offs.

text.p: The offer period for the transfer of equity to form the basis for the merger of two German banks began on Monday amid considerable interest from retail investors.
The offer is the first stage in the merger of Bayerischen Vereinsbank and Bayerischen Hypotheken- und Wechselbank which will ultimately create Germany's second largest commercial bank.
Shareholders in Hypo-Bank are being offered one share in insurance group Allianz AG for every six Hypo-Bank shares held.
The Allianz shares come from Vereinsbank's portfolio and will allow it to take up to 45 percent of Hypo-Bank.

A spokesman for Vereinsbank said on Monday that 500 people had called for detailed information by early afternoon on Monday, but addded that an initial report on the interest established would not be available until Tuesday.
The swap offer, which is valid from today up until September 10, had already received a notable level of interest from institutional investors, the spokesman said.

For the transaction to go ahead at least 40 percent of Hypo-Bank shareholders must take up the offer, which has been recommended by the management boards of both banks. The deal must also be approved by the German cartel office.

Hypo-Bank shares, which rose about 30 percent when the deal was announced two weeks ago, closed 1.30 marks lower at 72.80 on Monday. The two boards have warned that collapse of the deal could mean the price increase would be reversed.
Allianz shares ended 10.50 marks lower at 445.
Shares which are not exchanged in this offer will be taken up in a later merger offer, terms for which have not yet been announced.
